claim: Context compaction alone is insufficient to enable a frontier coding agent (Opus 4.5 on the Claude Agent SDK) to complete a production-quality multi-session project from a high-level prompt; a dedicated harness layer with environment scaffolding is required on top of compaction.
stance_target: context management/compaction infrastructure alone is sufficient for continuous long-running agent operation
scope_conditions: Claude Agent SDK, Opus 4.5, full-stack web app build task (claude.ai clone), published Nov 26 2025
quoted_support: However, compaction isn't sufficient. Out of the box, even a frontier coding model like Opus 4.5 running on the Claude Agent SDK in a loop across multiple context windows will fall short of building a production-quality web app if it's only given a high-level prompt.

claim: A two-agent harness pattern -- a one-time Initializer Agent that scaffolds the environment (init.sh, progress log, initial git commit, structured feature-requirements file) followed by a Coding Agent that runs every subsequent session -- resolves the 'no memory between sessions' problem of long-running agents.
stance_target: Director/Worker-style multi-agent architecture for continuous, multi-session autonomous software development
scope_conditions: Anthropic internal experiments on Claude Agent SDK
quoted_support: Initializer agent: The very first agent session uses a specialized prompt that asks the model to set up the initial environment... Coding agent: Every subsequent session asks the model to make incremental progress, then leave structured updates.

claim: Encoding the feature/requirements tracker as JSON rather than Markdown measurably reduced the model's tendency to inappropriately edit, remove, or overwrite the tracking file, because strongly-worded instructions plus JSON structure made unauthorized edits less likely.
stance_target: format choice for state-tracking artifacts affects agent compliance and audit integrity
quoted_support: After some experimentation, we landed on using JSON for this, as the model is less likely to inappropriately change or overwrite JSON files compared to Markdown files.

claim: Without explicit prompting to test end-to-end using browser automation tools acting as a human user would, a coding agent will mark features complete based on passing unit tests or curl checks alone and fail to recognize that the feature does not actually work end-to-end.
stance_target: unit-test-level verification is sufficient for rigid evals / zero-hallucination quality control in agentic coding loops
scope_conditions: Claude Agent SDK building a web application, using Puppeteer MCP for browser automation
quoted_support: Absent explicit prompting, Claude tended to make code changes, and even do testing with unit tests or curl commands against a development server, but would fail recognize that the feature didn't work end-to-end.

claim: Two concrete failure modes were observed in long-running agents without harness scaffolding: (1) the agent attempts to one-shot the entire task, running out of context mid-implementation and leaving the next session to guess at undocumented half-finished work, and (2) a later session observes partial progress and prematurely declares the overall project complete.
stance_target: specific, named failure modes that the zero-hallucination/quality-control pillar must design against in multi-session agentic loops
scope_conditions: Claude Agent SDK, full-stack app build
quoted_support: First, the agent tended to try to do too much at once—essentially to attempt to one-shot the app... A second failure mode would often occur later in a project. After some features had already been built, a later agent instance would look around, see that progress had been made, and declare the job done.

claim: It remains an open research question whether a single general-purpose coding agent or a multi-agent architecture (dedicated testing agent, QA agent, code-cleanup agent) performs best for long-horizon software development tasks across many context windows.
stance_target: whether specialization (multi-agent 'departments') or a generalist agent is the superior architecture for the software-factory loop
scope_conditions: stated as future work by Anthropic researchers
quoted_support: Most notably, it's still unclear whether a single, general-purpose coding agent performs best across contexts, or if better performance can be achieved through a multi-agent architecture. It seems reasonable that specialized agents like a testing agent, a quality assurance agent, or a code cleanup agent, could do an even better job at sub-tasks.
